title: SignDrop Zero-Day Turns Windows CLFS Defense Into Privilege Escalation
content_md: Key Findings SignDrop is a local privilege escalation from a standard user to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM targeting Microsoft's own CLFS authentication mitigation. The exploit was published on November 10, 2026, under the MSNightmare handle on GitHub. No coordinated disclosure, no CVE, no patch. The vulnerability turns a defense into an attack surface. Microsoft added HMAC-based authentication codes to CLFS log files specifically to block the class of logic bugs caused by improper validation of CLFS data structures, which accounted for 19 of 24 CLFS CVEs over five years. SignDrop abuses the signing mechanism itself: it forces clfs.sys to create a .cnpf signature file as SYSTEM in an attacker-controlled location, producing a privileged file-creation primitive at an attacker-selected path. Because the resulting file retains attacker-accessible security attributes, the exploit reopens it and replaces the CLFS-generated content with an embedded payload DLL. Microsoft Defender performs the privileged action on the attacker's behalf. The exploit calls Defender's signature update RPC interface to trigger a CLFS log open under SYSTEM context.
